audit.summary: A valid one-step AGT sparse-grid certificate yields a direct violation of the claimed pure-DP inequality after binary thresholding. A separate final-batch policy yields a false stability certificate on adjacent20/19-record datasets. Pointwise sensitivity and per-batch gradient bounds survive bounded checks.
limitations: P1 — Pointwise sensitivity upper bound lacks required neighboring-dataset smoothness — Counterevidence: Theorem5.1 pointwise bound remains valid and intervals are sound; exact maximal true radius has smoothness unavailable to incomplete/grid-rounded certificates. Witness does not claim historical datasets instantiate it.

P2 — Neighboring dataset can change update count and escape certified interval — Counterevidence: Main experiments use maximum/full batches, which can avoid this particular boundary. Per-batch bounds are sound. A properly coupled fixed update schedule could support a restricted theorem.
Limitations: No author-code execution, training, dataset/checkpoint download or empirical replication.
Limitations: Current public release not certified historical experiment identity.
Limitations: No formal floating-point soundness guarantee, external-proof audit or later-version review.

repair.content:
Prove smoothness of computable noise scale, use exact stable radius, globally smooth the bound, or develop another valid mechanism. Reassess utility at valid privacy budgets.

Specify and enforce neighboring-dataset-consistent step/batch schedule or enclose changed update counts; removing skip alone does not fix extra-step possibility.
